title.zh: 卷四十一 列傳第十一 魏舒 李憙 劉寔 高光
title.en: Volume 41 Biographies 11: Wei Shu; Li Xi; Liu Shi; Gao Guang
title.raw: 卷四十一 列傳第十一 魏舒 李憙 劉寔 高光 Volume 41 Biographies 11: Wei Shu; Li Xi; Liu Shi; Gao Guang

sentences.zh: 魏舒，字陽元，任城樊人也。

translations.literal: Wei Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was a man of Fan in Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu, whose courtesy name was Yangyuan, came from Fan in Rencheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 少孤，為外家寧氏所養。

translations.literal: He was orphaned young and was raised by his maternal grandparents' Ning clan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned while still a boy, he was brought up in the household of his mother's people, the Nings.

sentences.zh: 寧氏起宅，相宅者云：「當出貴甥。

translations.literal: When the Ning family built a house, the geomancer said: "A noble nephew will issue from this."
translations.idiomatic: As the Nings raised a new residence, a geomancer told them it would produce a distinguished nephew.

sentences.zh: 」外祖母以魏氏甥小而慧，意謂應之。

translations.literal: His maternal grandmother, taking the Wei nephew to be young yet clever, thought it referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandmother, seeing the Wei boy as bright despite his youth, assumed the prophecy pointed to him.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「當為外氏成此宅相。

translations.literal: Shu said: "It will be for the maternal house to fulfill this house omen."
translations.idiomatic: Shu replied, "Then it falls to our mother's family to make good on that sign."

sentences.zh: 」久乃別居。

translations.literal: Only after a long time did he separate and live apart.
translations.idiomatic: Only much later did he move out and establish a separate household.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺二寸，姿望秀偉，飲酒石餘，而遲鈍質樸，不為鄉親所重。

translations.literal: He was eight chi two cun in height, of fine and imposing bearing, and could drink over a picul of wine; yet he was slow, dull, and plain, and was not esteemed by his fellow villagers.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi two cun tall, cut a striking figure, and could put away more than a picul of wine, yet he seemed slow and unpolished, so neighbors and kin thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 從叔父吏部郎衡，有名當世，亦不之知，使守水碓，每歎曰：「舒堪數百戶長，我願畢矣！

translations.literal: His father's cousin Heng, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was celebrated in his age, yet he too did not recognize Shu's abilities, and set him to tend the water-powered mill. He would often sigh, saying: "Shu would make a hundred-household chief at best—that would be the limit of my hopes!"
translations.idiomatic: His father's cousin Heng, a celebrated Director of Personnel, never saw his talent either and put him in charge of the water mill, sighing that if Shu could manage a few hundred households his own ambitions would be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 」舒亦不以介意。

translations.literal: Shu likewise did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Shu did not let it trouble him.

sentences.zh: 不修常人之節，不為皎曆之事，每欲容才長物，終不顯人之短。

translations.literal: He did not cultivate the conventional sense of decorum, nor did he pursue showy, ostentatious conduct; he always wished to tolerate talent and nurture others, and never exposed people's shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: He neither fussed over petty proprieties nor sought flashy renown; he preferred to make room for others' gifts and never aired their faults.

sentences.zh: 性好騎射，著韋衣。

translations.literal: He was fond of horsemanship and archery and wore leather garments.
translations.idiomatic: He loved riding and archery and went about in leather hunting dress.

sentences.zh: 入山澤，以漁獵為事。

translations.literal: He went into the mountains and marshes and made fishing and hunting his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his time in hills and wetlands, fishing and hunting for a living.

sentences.zh: 唯太原王乂謂舒曰：「卿終當為台輔，然今未能令妻子免饑寒，吾當助卿營之。

translations.literal: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan said to Shu: "You will in the end become a pillar of the state, but for now you cannot keep your wife and children free from hunger and cold—I shall help you provide for them."
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan told him, "You are destined for the highest councils, yet today you cannot keep your household from want; I will help you see to their needs."

sentences.zh: 」常振其匱乏，舒受而不辭。

translations.literal: He often supplied his wants; Shu accepted without declining.
translations.idiomatic: Wang regularly relieved his straits, and Shu accepted without demur.

sentences.zh: 舒嘗詣野王，主人妻夜產，俄而聞車馬之聲，相問曰：「男也，女也？

translations.literal: Shu once went to Yewang; the host's wife gave birth at night, and presently they heard the sound of horses and chariots, and voices asked one another, "Boy or girl?"
translations.idiomatic: Once when Shu was staying in Yewang, the host's wife labored at night; soon the clatter of horses and wheels was heard, and voices called back and forth: a boy or a girl?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「男，書之，十五以兵死。

translations.literal: They said: "A boy—record it: he will die by arms at fifteen."
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: a boy—write it down—he will die by the sword at fifteen.

sentences.zh: 」復問：「寢者為誰？

translations.literal: They asked again: "Who is the one sleeping here?"
translations.idiomatic: Then they asked who was sleeping in the house.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「魏公舒。

translations.literal: They said: "Lord Wei Shu."
translations.idiomatic: "Wei Shu," came the reply.

sentences.zh: 」後十五載，詣主人，問所生兒何在，曰：「因條桑為斧傷而死。

translations.literal: Fifteen years later he called on the host and asked where the child was; the reply was, "He died from an axe wound while pruning mulberry."
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years later Shu looked up his host and asked after the child; the man said the boy had been killed by an axe while trimming mulberry.

sentences.zh: 」舒自知當為公矣。

translations.literal: Shu knew for himself that he was destined to become a duke (gong).
translations.idiomatic: Shu understood then that he was fated to rise to the rank of duke.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，郡上計掾察孝廉。

translations.literal: In his forties, the commandery nominated him as clerk for the annual account and recommended him Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: After he turned forty, the commandery sent him up as accounts clerk and nominated him Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 宗党以舒無學業，勸令不就，可以為高耳。

translations.literal: His clan and associates, because Shu had no scholarly learning, urged him not to accept—it could count as lofty conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen thought him without book learning and urged him to stay home, which would look admirably high-minded.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「若試而不中，其負在我，安可虛竊不就之高以為己榮乎！

translations.literal: Shu said: "If I try the examination and do not pass, the fault is mine—how could I vainly steal the reputation of not going for loftiness' sake!"
translations.idiomatic: Shu answered, "If I sit the exam and fail, the blame is mine; I will not borrow a false reputation by refusing what I have not earned."

sentences.zh: 」於是自課。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set himself to study.
translations.idiomatic: He then imposed a strict course of study on himself.

sentences.zh: 百日習一經，因而對策升第。

translations.literal: In a hundred days he mastered one classic and thereby passed the policy session and rose in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Within a hundred days he had worked through one classic, passed the palace examination, and won placement.

sentences.zh: 除澠池長，遷浚儀令，入為尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Mianchi, promoted to magistrate of Junyi, and entered the capital as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was named magistrate of Mianchi, then of Junyi, and finally entered court service as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時欲沙汰郎官。

translations.literal: At that time they wished to weed out the Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: A purge of the gentleman clerks was under way.

sentences.zh: 非其才者罷之。

translations.literal: Those without the requisite talent were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone judged unfit was to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「吾即其人也。

translations.literal: Shu said: "I am such a one."
translations.idiomatic: "I am one of those," said Shu.

sentences.zh: 」襆被而出。

translations.literal: He bundled his bedding and left.
translations.idiomatic: He rolled up his bedding and walked out.

sentences.zh: 同僚素無清論者咸有愧色，談者稱之。

translations.literal: Colleagues who had never been known for upright discourse all felt ashamed; commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow officials who had never passed for men of principle colored with shame, while observers praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 累遷後將軍鐘毓長史，毓每與參佐射，舒常為畫籌而已。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to senior major to General of the Rear Zhong Yu; whenever Yu gathered his staff for archery, Shu merely kept score for them.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted in stages to chief clerk under General of the Rear Zhong Yu, Shu usually only tallied arrows when Yu and his aides shot for sport.

sentences.zh: 後遇朋人不足，以舒滿數。

translations.literal: Later, when the party fell short of people, they filled the number with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Once the archery party lacked a man, they added Shu to round out the teams.

sentences.zh: 毓初不知其善射。

translations.literal: Yu at first did not know he was skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu had not known he could shoot.

sentences.zh: 舒容范閒雅，發無不中，舉坐愕然。

translations.literal: Shu's demeanor was relaxed and refined; every shot struck true, and the whole company was stunned.
translations.idiomatic: Shu stood at ease, every arrow found its mark, and the company sat thunderstruck.

sentences.zh: 莫有敵者。

translations.literal: There was no one who could match him.
translations.idiomatic: No one there could rival him.

sentences.zh: 毓歎而謝曰：「吾之不足以盡卿才，有如此射矣，豈一事哉！

translations.literal: Yu sighed and apologized, saying: "My failure to exhaust your talents is like this in archery alone—could it be only in this one thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu sighed and apologized: "If I have failed to use your gifts fully, archery alone proves it—this cannot be the only field."

sentences.zh: 」轉相國參軍，封劇陽子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to adviser to the minister of state and enfeoffed as Baron of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to adviser on the minister of state's staff and enfeoffed as Baron of Juyang.

sentences.zh: 府朝碎務，未嘗見是非；

translations.literal: In the routine affairs of the bureau he never showed approval or disapproval;
translations.idiomatic: On petty bureau business he never tipped his hand;

sentences.zh: 至於廢興大事，眾人莫能斷者，舒徐為籌之，多出眾議之表。

translations.literal: as for weighty matters of abolition and establishment, where the crowd could not decide, Shu would slowly work out a plan for them, often surpassing what the assembly had said.
translations.idiomatic: yet on great questions of state that left the staff divided, he would quietly think them through and often outstrip every other proposal.

sentences.zh: 文帝深器重之，每朝會坐罷，目送之曰：「魏舒堂堂，人之領袖也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen thought very highly of him; whenever court adjourned he would watch him go and say: "Wei Shu is imposing—the leader among men."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao) valued him deeply; as court broke up he would watch Shu leave and murmur, "Wei Shu has true presence—he is the sort men follow."

sentences.zh: 」遷宜陽、滎陽二郡太守，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor of the two commanderies Yiyang and Xingyang, where he enjoyed a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Yiyang and Xingyang, earning wide acclaim in both posts.

sentences.zh: 徵拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州刺史，在州三年，以簡惠稱。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Ji Province; during three years in the province he was praised for simplicity and benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as provincial inspector of Ji, he governed three years and was known for a light touch and humane rule.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中。

translations.literal: He entered the court as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武帝以舒清素，特賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, because Shu was clear-minded and unassuming, specially gifted him a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, noting his austerity, presented him with a hundred bolts of silk as a special mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書，以公事當免官，詔以贖論。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Masters of Writing; on official grounds he should have been removed from office, but an edict ruled he could redeem the penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to Masters of Writing, he faced dismissal over an official matter; an edict allowed him to commute the penalty with a fine.

sentences.zh: 舒三娶妻皆亡，是歲自表乞假還本郡葬妻，詔賜葬地一頃，錢五十萬。

translations.literal: Shu had three wives, all of whom died; that year he petitioned to return to his home commandery on leave to bury his wife; an edict granted burial land of one hundred mu and cash of five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: All three of Shu's wives had died; that year he asked leave to go home and bury the last, and the throne granted him a hectare of burial ground and half a million cash.

sentences.zh: 太康初，拜右僕射。

translations.literal: At the start of the Taikang era he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taikang era he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 舒與衛瓘、山濤、張華等以六合混一，宜用古典封禪東嶽，前後累陳其事，帝謙讓不許。

translations.literal: Shu with Wei Guan, Shan Tao, Zhang Hua, and others argued that with the six directions united in one, the classical rite of feng and shan on the eastern march should be used; they presented the matter repeatedly, but the emperor modestly declined permission.
translations.idiomatic: Shu joined Wei Guan, Shan Tao, Zhang Hua, and others in urging that, with the realm reunited, the court ought to perform the classical Feng and Shan sacrifices on Mount Tai; they memorialized again and again, but the emperor modestly refused.

sentences.zh: 以舒為左僕射，領吏部。

translations.literal: Shu was appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, concurrent with heading the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat with acting charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 舒上言：「今選六宮，聘以玉帛，而舊使禦府丞奉聘，宣成嘉禮，贄重使輕。

translations.literal: Shu presented a memorial: "In selecting the six palaces they use jade and silk for the betrothal, yet the old practice sends the assistant director of the imperial workshops to deliver the betrothal gifts—thus the auspicious rite is proclaimed, yet the tribute is weighty and the envoy light."
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized: "Palace ladies are chosen with jade and silk as bride-price, yet we still send the assistant from the imperial workshops to carry the gifts—the ritual is grand but the envoy beneath it."

sentences.zh: 以為拜三夫人宜使卿，九嬪使五官中郎將，美人、良人使謁者，於典制為弘。

translations.literal: "We deem that for investing the Three Ladies of highest rank envoys of minister rank should be sent; for the Nine Concubines the leader of court gentlemen for domestic service; for the Beauties and the Worthies officials from the reception office—thus the regulation would be more ample."
translations.idiomatic: "Investitures of the Three Ladies should go through ministers, the Nine Concubines through the leader of court gentlemen for domestic service, the Beauties and Worthies through reception officers—then the statutes would match the dignity of the rite."

sentences.zh: 」有詔詳之，眾議異同，遂寢。

translations.literal: An edict ordered detailed consideration; the assembly's views diverged, and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered study, opinions split, and the proposal lapsed.

sentences.zh: 加右光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Grand Master of the Right and ceremonial parity with the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally named Grand Master of the Right with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 及山濤薨，以舒領司徒，有頃即真。

translations.literal: When Shan Tao died, Shu was placed in charge of the Minister of Education and shortly after confirmed in full office.
translations.idiomatic: When Shan Tao died, Shu took provisional charge of the Ministry of Education and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 舒有威重德望，祿賜散之九族，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Shu had august dignity and moral prestige; he distributed stipends and gifts among his entire clan and left no surplus wealth at home.
translations.idiomatic: A man of formidable presence and reputation, he shared every stipend and gift with his extended kin and kept nothing in reserve.

sentences.zh: 陳留周震累為諸府所辟，辟書既下，公輒喪亡，僉號震為殺公掾，莫有辟者。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhen of Chenliu was repeatedly summoned by various offices; as soon as the letter of appointment arrived, the lord would die, and all called Zhen the "clerk who kills lords"—no one would employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhen of Chenliu had been summoned to several bureaus, yet each time the commission arrived his new chief died; people called him the clerk who killed his superiors, and no one would hire him.

sentences.zh: 舒乃命之，而竟無患，識者以此稱其達命。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon gave him an appointment, and in the end no misfortune occurred—thoughtful men praised this as his grasp of fate.
translations.idiomatic: Shu offered him a post anyway, and no calamity followed; observers said this showed his understanding of destiny.

sentences.zh: 以年老，每稱疾遜位。

translations.literal: On account of old age he often pleaded illness to yield his post.
translations.idiomatic: Growing old, he repeatedly cited illness to resign.

sentences.zh: 中復暫起，署兗州中正，尋又稱疾。

translations.literal: In the interim he briefly took office again as impartial judge for Yan Province, then again pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly returned to serve as provincial personnel evaluator for Yan, then pleaded illness again.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞郤詵與舒書曰：「公久疾小差，視事是也，唯上所念。

translations.literal: Xi Shen, Assistant Director of the Left of the Masters of Writing, wrote to Shu: "Your long illness has lifted a little; attending to duties is appropriate—only bear in mind what the sovereign is concerned about."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shen, assistant director on the left of the Masters of Writing, wrote: "Your long illness has eased; resuming duty would be right—only the throne's wishes matter."

sentences.zh: 何竟起訖還臥，曲身回法，甚失具瞻之望。

translations.literal: "Why rise and at once return to bed, twisting body and bending law—it greatly disappoints those who look up to you."
translations.idiomatic: "To rise only to go straight back to bed, bending every rule, betrays what the realm expects of you."

sentences.zh: 公少立巍巍，一旦棄之，可不惜哉！

translations.literal: "You stood toweringly in youth; to cast it away in a day—how regrettable!"
translations.idiomatic: "You built a towering name in your prime; to throw it away now would be a waste beyond words."

sentences.zh: 」舒稱疾如初。

translations.literal: Shu pleaded illness as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shu again pleaded illness as he had before.

sentences.zh: 後以災異遜位，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Later, citing strange portents, he yielded his place; the emperor did not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: He later cited ill omens to step down; the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 後因正旦朝罷還第，表送章綬。

translations.literal: Later, when court for New Year's Day had ended and he returned to his residence, he submitted his seals and cords.
translations.idiomatic: After New Year's court he went home and returned his seals of office.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔敦勉。

translations.literal: The emperor by his own hand issued an edict earnestly urging him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a personal edict urging him to remain.

sentences.zh: 而舒執意彌固，乃下詔曰：「司徒、劇陽子舒，體道弘粹，思量經遠，忠肅居正，在公盡規。

translations.literal: Yet Shu held all the firmer to his purpose, so an edict was issued: "The Minister of Education, Baron of Ju Shu, embodies the Way in breadth and purity, thinks far and plans deeply, is loyal and grave and holds the upright course, and in public service fully remonstrates."
translations.idiomatic: Shu would not budge, so the court proclaimed: "Minister of Education and Baron of Juyang, Wei Shu, embodies the Way in its breadth and purity, plans with a long view, serves with loyal gravity, and in office never fails to speak plain truth."

sentences.zh: 入管銓衡，官人允敘；

translations.literal: "Within he managed the balance of appointments and ordered officials fittingly;"
translations.idiomatic: "Within the capital he ran appointments and ranked officials fairly;"

sentences.zh: 出贊袞職，敷弘五教。

translations.literal: "without he assisted the Three Dukes and spread the five teachings."
translations.idiomatic: "beyond it he aided the highest ministers and spread the five teachings abroad."

sentences.zh: 惠訓播流，德聲茂著，可謂朝之俊乂者也。

translations.literal: "His kindly instruction flowed abroad and his virtuous name flourished—he may be called a pillar of the court."
translations.idiomatic: "His gentle counsel has gone out like water, and his virtue is renowned—he is truly one of the court's great pillars."

sentences.zh: 而屢執沖讓，辭旨懇誠，申覽反覆，省用憮然。

translations.literal: "Yet repeatedly he pressed humble refusal, his wording earnest and sincere; our repeated reading leaves us sorrowful."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet he has pressed his modest retirements again and again in language so earnest that each reading leaves us troubled."

sentences.zh: 蓋成人之美，先典所與，難違至情。

translations.literal: "As for fulfilling another's good desire, the former canons endorse it—it is hard to gainsay so deep a feeling."
translations.idiomatic: "The classics bless us when we honor another man's chosen course; deep feeling is not lightly refused."

sentences.zh: 今聽其所執，以劇陽子就第，位同三司，祿賜如前。

translations.literal: "Now we accede to what he holds to: let the Baron of Ju retire to his estate with rank equal to the Three Dukes, stipends and gifts as before."
translations.idiomatic: "We therefore grant his wish: the Baron of Juyang may retire to private life with rank matching the Three Dukes and keep his former salary and perquisites."

sentences.zh: 几杖不朝，賜錢百萬，床帳簟褥自副。

translations.literal: "He need not attend court with staff and cushion; we grant a million in cash, with bed-curtains, bed-mats, and bedding complete."
translations.idiomatic: "He is excused from court even on staff-and-cushion occasions; we add a million cash, with bed hangings, mats, and bedding supplied in full."

sentences.zh: 以舍人四人為劇陽子舍人，置官騎十人。

translations.literal: "Four yeomen are assigned as household yeomen to the Baron of Ju, with ten mounted attendants."
translations.idiomatic: "Four household gentlemen will attend the baronial household, with ten official escort riders."

sentences.zh: 使光祿勳奉策，主者詳案典禮，令皆如舊制。

translations.literal: "Let the Master of Ceremonies present the document, and let those in charge review the rules of ceremony so that all follows the old statutes."
translations.idiomatic: "The Master of Ceremonies shall deliver the patent; bureaus are to check precedent so every detail follows standing ritual."

sentences.zh: 」於是賜安車駟馬，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was given a secure carriage and four horses, and staves blocking the carriage approach before his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He received a secure carriage, a four-horse team, and the crossbars before his gate that mark ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 舒為事必先行而後言，遜位之際，莫有知者。

translations.literal: Shu with matters always acted first and spoke afterward; when he yielded his office, no one knew beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Shu always acted before he spoke; when he resigned, no one had seen it coming.

sentences.zh: 時論以為晉興以來，三公能辭榮善終者，未之有也。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion held that since the rise of Jin, no one among the Three Dukes had been able to renounce glory and end well—until then.
translations.idiomatic: People said that since the Jin dynasty began, no Three Duke had ever surrendered honor and finished his days in peace—until Shu.

sentences.zh: 司空衛瓘與舒書曰：「每與足下共論此事，日日未果，可謂瞻之在前，忽焉在後矣。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wei Guan wrote to Shu: "Whenever I discussed this with you, day after day it never came to pass—as if present before the eyes, then suddenly gone behind."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Wei Guan wrote: "We spoke of this again and again, yet each day it remained undone—always seeming within reach, then slipping away."

sentences.zh: 」太熙元年薨，時年八十二。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Taixi, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Taixi era, aged eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 帝甚傷悼，賵賻優厚，諡曰康。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved deeply and gave generous funeral gifts; his posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply, sent lavish funeral goods, and gave him the posthumous name Kang, "Peaceful."

sentences.zh: 子混，字延廣，清惠有才行，為太子舍人。

translations.literal: His son Hun, courtesy name Yanguang, was pure-minded, generous, and capable; he served as Household Gentleman to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hun, courtesy name Yanguang, was clear-minded, generous, and talented, and served as gentleman attendant on the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 年二十七，先舒卒，朝野咸為舒悲惜。

translations.literal: At twenty-seven he died before Shu; court and countryside alike grieved for Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-seven, before his father; court and capital alike grieved for the old man.

sentences.zh: 舒每哀慟，退而歎曰：「吾不及莊生遠矣，豈以無益自損乎！

translations.literal: Shu would mourn bitterly, then withdraw and sigh, saying: "How far I fall short of Master Zhuang—would I harm myself for something unprofitable!"
translations.idiomatic: Shu mourned fiercely, then withdrew and sighed, "I am nothing beside Master Zhuang—why should I injure myself for what cannot help?"

sentences.zh: 」於是終服不復哭。

translations.literal: Thereupon he completed mourning and wept no more.
translations.idiomatic: After that he finished the mourning rites and did not weep again.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「舒惟一子，薄命短折。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Shu had but one son, fated to a short and broken life."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Shu had only one son, and fate cut him off young."

sentences.zh: 舒告老之年，處窮獨之苦，每念怛然，為之嗟悼。

translations.literal: In the years when Shu petitioned to retire, he suffered the bitterness of utter bereavement; each time we think of it our heart aches, and we sigh in sorrow for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the years when he seeks to step down he endures the bitterness of solitude without heir; the thought pains us, and we grieve for him.

sentences.zh: 思所以散愁養氣，可更增滋味品物。

translations.literal: We wish thereby to dispel care and nourish his spirits—let the variety of fine foods be increased for him.
translations.idiomatic: We would find ways to ease his sorrow and restore his strength—let richer foods and dainties be added to his table.

sentences.zh: 仍給賜陽燧四望繐窗戶皁輪車牛一乘，庶出入觀望，或足散憂也。

translations.literal: In addition grant a four-windowed gauze coach with sun-striker, black-wheeled ox-cart and one pair of oxen, so that going out he may look about and perhaps ease his sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Further grant him a carriage fitted with a bronze fire-mirror, four gauze windows, black wheels, and a yoke of oxen, so he may ride out, take in the view, and perhaps lighten his grief.

sentences.zh: 」以庶孫融嗣。

translations.literal: He was succeeded by his grandson by a concubine, Rong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Rong, born of a concubine's line, was named heir.

sentences.zh: 又早卒，從孫晃嗣。

translations.literal: Rong also died young; he was succeeded by a grand-nephew, Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong also died young, and a grand-nephew, Huang, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 李憙，字季和，上黨銅鞮人也。

translations.literal: Li Xi, courtesy name Jihe, was a man of Tongdi in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi, courtesy name Jihe, was a native of Tongdi in Shangdang commandery.

sentences.zh: 父牷，漢大鴻臚。

translations.literal: His father Quan held the post of Grand Herald in Han.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Li Quan, had been Grand Herald under the Han.

sentences.zh: 憙少有高行，博學研精，與北海管甯以賢良征，不行。

translations.literal: Xi in youth had lofty conduct, was broad in learning and drilled in essentials, and with Guan Ning of Beihai was summoned as Worthy and Good—he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he carried himself with uncommon rectitude, read widely and to the point, and when he and Guan Ning of Beihai were summoned together as men of worth, he did not go.

sentences.zh: 累辟三府，不就。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly summoned by the Three Offices but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Offices called him repeatedly; he declined each time.

sentences.zh: 宣帝復辟憙為太傅屬，固辭疾，郡縣扶輿上道，時憙母疾篤，乃竊逾泫氏城而徒還，遂遭母喪，論者嘉其志節。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan (Sima Yi) again summoned Xi as an assistant to the Grand Tutor; he firmly declined on grounds of illness. The commandery and county had him carried in a litter onto the road; at the time Xi's mother was gravely ill, so he stole away over the wall of Xuanshi City and returned on foot, and then met his mother's death. Commentators praised his integrity and resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan summoned him as an aide to the Grand Tutor; he pleaded illness and refused, but local officials forced him into a litter. His mother lay dying, so he slipped over the wall at Xuanshi and walked home; she died soon after, and observers praised his steadfast devotion.

sentences.zh: 後為并州別駕，時驍騎將軍秦朗過并州，州將畢軌敬焉。

translations.literal: Later he became chief clerk for Bing Province; at the time General of Agile Cavalry Qin Lang passed through Bing Province, and the provincial commander Bi Gui honored him.
translations.idiomatic: He later became chief clerk of Bing Province; when General of Agile Cavalry Qin Lang passed through, provincial commander Bi Gui treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 令乘車至閣。

translations.literal: He ordered him to ride in a carriage to the gate-tower chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xi brought by carriage right to the vestibule.

sentences.zh: 憙固諫以為不可，軌不得已從之。

translations.literal: Xi firmly remonstrated that it should not be done; Gui had no choice but to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Xi argued firmly against the honor; Bi Gui yielded only because he had to.

sentences.zh: 景帝輔政，命憙為大將軍從事中郎，憙到，引見，謂憙曰：「昔先公辟君而君不應，今孤命君而君至，何也？

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing (Sima Shi) held the regency, he appointed Xi as a staff adviser to the general-in-chief. When Xi arrived and was granted audience, he said to Xi: "Formerly my father summoned you and you did not respond; now I command you and you have come—why is that?"
translations.idiomatic: Regent Emperor Jing named him adviser on the general-in-chief's staff. At their first meeting he asked, "Your father once called you forth and you stayed away; I summon you and you appear—what changed?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「先君以禮見待，憙得以禮進退。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your late father treated me with ritual propriety; I was able to advance or withdraw according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Xi answered, "Your father received me with courtesy, so I could answer with courtesy—coming or staying away."

sentences.zh: 明公以法見繩，憙畏法而至。

translations.literal: Your enlightened lordship binds me with the law; I fear the law and therefore have come."
translations.idiomatic: You hold me to the law; I come because I fear it."

sentences.zh: 」帝甚重之。

translations.literal: The emperor thought very highly of him.
translations.idiomatic: The regent esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 轉司馬，尋拜右長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be marshal and soon appointed senior clerk on the right.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the marshal's office and was soon named senior clerk on the right.

sentences.zh: 從討毌丘儉還，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He returned from the campaign against Guanqiu Jian and was promoted to palace assistant secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign against Guanqiu Jian he was raised to palace assistant secretary.

sentences.zh: 當官正色，不憚強禦，百僚震肅焉。

translations.literal: In office he was stern of mien and did not fear the powerful; the hundred officials were awed into discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He held his post with unflinching dignity and showed no fear of the mighty; the whole bureaucracy stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 薦樂安孫璞，亦以道德顯，時人稱為知人。

translations.literal: He recommended Sun Pu of Le'an, who likewise became eminent through moral conduct; people of the time called him one who knew men.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Sun Pu of Le'an, who likewise won fame on moral grounds; contemporaries said he had an eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 尋遷大司馬，以公事免。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to Grand Marshal, then removed on official grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he rose to Grand Marshal, only to be dismissed over an official matter.

sentences.zh: 司馬伷為甯北將軍，鎮鄴，以憙為軍司。

translations.literal: When Sima Zhou was General Who Guards the North and garrisoned Ye, he made Xi his army director.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhou, as General Who Guards the North at Ye, appointed him army director.

sentences.zh: 頃之，除涼州刺史，加揚威將軍、假節，領護羌校尉，綏禦華夷，甚有聲績。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed inspector of Liang Province, given the additional title General Who Spreads Might and credential staff, and concurrent colonel of Qiang auxiliaries; he pacified Chinese and barbarian alike and achieved a notable record.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after he became inspector of Liang, with the added rank of General Who Spreads Might, ceremonial axe, and concurrent Qiang command—he kept Hu and Han in order and earned wide praise.

sentences.zh: 羌虜犯塞，憙因其隙會，不及啟聞，輒以便宜出軍深入，遂大克獲，以功重免譴，時人比之漢朝馮、甘焉。

translations.literal: When Qiang raiders violated the passes, Xi seized the opportunity; without waiting to report, he on his own authority sent the army deep and won a great victory. Because the merit outweighed the fault he escaped punishment, and people of the time compared him to Feng and Gan of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang raiders broke the frontier; Xi acted on the opening without awaiting orders, drove deep, and routed them. Merit outweighed breach of protocol, so he went unpunished, and men likened him to Feng Fengshi and Gan Yanshou of Han.

sentences.zh: 於是請還，許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested to return; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire from the frontier, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 居家月餘，拜冀州刺史，累遷司隸校尉。

translations.literal: After more than a month at home he was appointed inspector of Ji Province and was promoted in stages to metropolitan commandant.
translations.idiomatic: A month at home, then appointment as inspector of Ji; step by step he rose to metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 及魏帝告禪于晉，憙以本官行司徒事，副太尉鄭沖奉策。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor announced abdication to Jin, Xi, in his current office, acted for the minister of education and, as deputy to Grand Commandant Zheng Chong, presented the document of investiture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei throne yielded to Jin, he discharged the minister of education's duties in his existing rank and, assisting Grand Commandant Zheng Chong, presented the abdication patent.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，封祁侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taishi era he was enfeoffed as marquis of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he received the marquisate of Qi.

sentences.zh: 憙上言：「故立進令劉友、前尚書山濤、中山王睦、故尚書僕射武陔各占官三更稻田，請免濤、睦等官。

translations.literal: Xi presented a memorial: "The late director of Lijin Liu You, former Masters of Writing Shan Tao, Prince Mu of Zhongshan, and the late vice director of the Masters of Writing Wu Gai each occupied three qing of official rice paddy; I ask that Tao, Mu, and the others be removed from office."
translations.idiomatic: Xi reported that Liu You, Shan Tao, Prince Mu of Zhongshan, and the late Wu Gai had each seized three qing of government paddy; he asked that Shan Tao and the prince be stripped of their posts.

sentences.zh: 陔已亡，請貶諡。

translations.literal: Gai is already dead; I ask that his posthumous title be degraded.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Gai being dead, he asked that his posthumous name be lowered.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「法者，天下取正，不避親貴，然後行耳，吾豈將枉縱其間哉！

translations.literal: An edict said: "The law is what the realm takes as its standard; it must not shrink from kin or the noble—only then is it enforced. Would I bend or indulge in between!"
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Law is the measure of the empire; it must spare neither kin nor grandees—or it is nothing. I will not twist it for favor."

sentences.zh: 然案此事皆是友所作，侵剝百姓，以繆惑朝士。

translations.literal: Yet investigation shows this affair was all You's doing—he encroached on and exploited the common people and with falsehoods misled court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the inquiry showed Liu You alone had done it—preying on commoners and deceiving the court with lies.

sentences.zh: 奸吏乃敢作此，其考竟友以懲邪佞。

translations.literal: That a wicked clerk dared do this—interrogate You to the end to punish the crooked and sycophantic.
translations.idiomatic: Let that corrupt clerk be tried to the full sentence, to chastise treachery and flattery.

sentences.zh: 濤等不貳其過者，皆勿有所問。

translations.literal: As for Tao and the rest who did not double his offense, none shall be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao and others who did not share his guilt are not to be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱'王臣蹇蹇，匪躬之故'。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says, 'The king's ministers face hardship upon hardship—not for their own persons' sake.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says the king's ministers brave hardship—not for private ends.

sentences.zh: 今憙亢志在公，當官而行，可謂'邦之司直'者矣。

translations.literal: Now Xi uplifts his aim in the public good and carries out his office—he may be called 'the straightener of the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Xi sets the common good above himself and does the duty before him—he is the 'straight staff of the state.'

sentences.zh: 光武有云：'貴戚且斂手以避二鮑'。

translations.literal: Guangwu said, 'Let the imperial kin draw in their hands to give way to the two Baos.'
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu said the great families should stand aside for men like the two Baos.

sentences.zh: 豈其然乎！

translations.literal: Is it not indeed so!
translations.idiomatic: Is that not exactly our case?

sentences.zh: 其申敕群僚，各慎所司，寬宥之恩，不可數遇也。

translations.literal: Let this be sternly charged to the host of officials: each must be careful in his charge; the grace of leniency cannot be met with repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Charge every official to mind his brief—pardons must not become routine.

sentences.zh: 」憙為二代司隸，朝野稱之。

translations.literal: Xi served as metropolitan commandant under two dynasties; court and countryside praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi held the metropolitan inspectorship under two houses, and all the realm approved.

sentences.zh: 以公事免。

translations.literal: He was removed on official grounds.
translations.idiomatic: He stepped down over an official matter.

sentences.zh: 其年，皇太子立，以憙為太子太傅。

translations.literal: That year, when the heir apparent was installed, Xi was made grand tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The same year the crown prince was named, Xi became his grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 自魏明帝以後，久曠東宮，制度廢闕，官司不具，詹事、左右率、庶子、中舍人諸官並未置，唯置衛率令典兵，二傅並攝眾事。

translations.literal: From Emperor Ming of Wei onward, the eastern palace had long stood vacant; its institutions had fallen into disuse and its offices were incomplete—the steward, left and right leaders, household gentlemen, and inner gentlemen had all gone unappointed; only the commandant of guards was set to command troops, and the two tutors together handled all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei Mingdi the heir's residence had stood empty: regulations lapsed, posts went unfilled—no steward, no guard captains, no household staff—only a guard command held the troops while both tutors managed everything else.

sentences.zh: 憙在位累年，訓道盡規。

translations.literal: Xi held the post for many years, instructing and remonstrating to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Xi held the office for years, teaching the prince and speaking plainly whenever duty required.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書僕射，拜特進、光祿大夫，以年老遜位。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Masters of Writing, appointed specially advanced and grand master of splendid happiness, and on account of old age yielded his post.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the Masters of Writing, took the titles Specially Advanced and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then retired on grounds of age.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「光祿大夫、特進李憙，杖德居義，當升台司。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Specially Advanced Li Xi, relying on virtue and abiding in righteousness, ought to have ascended to the high ministers' bench."
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed: "Grand Master Li Xi, Specially Advanced, has leaned on virtue and kept to the right—he should have joined the highest council."

sentences.zh: 毗亮朕躬，而以年尊致仕。

translations.literal: "He has aided and illumined Our person, yet on account of advanced years has retired."
translations.idiomatic: "He has steadied Our rule, yet age has led him to retire."

sentences.zh: 雖優遊無為，可以頤神，而虛心之望，能不憮然！

translations.literal: "Though ease and inaction may nourish the spirit, how can Our longing for an empty mind not leave Us sorrowful!"
translations.idiomatic: "Leisure may restore him, but Our wish to keep him near leaves Us heavy-hearted."

sentences.zh: 其因光祿之號，改假金紫，置官騎十人，賜錢五十萬，祿賜班禮，一如三司，門施行馬。」

translations.literal: "Let him keep the title of grand master of splendid happiness but be given the gold seal and purple ribbon, ten mounted attendants, and cash of five hundred thousand; stipends, gifts, and court ritual shall match the Three Dukes, and staves shall block the approach before his gate."
translations.idiomatic: "Retain his splendid-happiness title, add the gold seal and purple ribbon, assign ten escort riders, grant half a million cash, and match the Three Dukes in salary, gifts, and ceremony, with crossbars before his gate."

sentences.zh: 初，憙為僕射時，涼州虜寇邊，憙唱義遣軍討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xi was vice director, barbarians raided the Liangzhou frontier; Xi was first to urge sending an army against them.
translations.idiomatic: While Xi served as vice director, tribes struck Liangzhou; he was the first to urge a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 朝士謂出兵不易，虜未足為患，竟不從之。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen said dispatching troops was no easy matter and the raiders were not enough to worry about; in the end they did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers called war too costly and the raiders a minor nuisance; they ignored him.

sentences.zh: 後虜果大縱逸，涼州覆沒，朝廷深悔焉。

translations.literal: Later the barbarians indeed ran rampant, Liangzhou was overrun, and the court deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes then swept the frontier, Liangzhou collapsed, and the court bitterly regretted its refusal.

sentences.zh: 以憙清素貧儉，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Because Xi was clear-minded, plain, and poor in his frugality, he was gifted a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his austerity and want, the throne sent him a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 及齊王攸出鎮，憙上疏諫爭，辭甚懇切。

translations.literal: When Prince You of Qi went out to a border command, Xi submitted a memorial remonstrating; the wording was very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince You of Qi was sent to hold a frontier post, Xi memorialized in blunt, heartfelt protest.

sentences.zh: 憙自曆仕，雖清非異眾，而家無儲積，親舊故人乃至分衣共食，未嘗私以王官。

translations.literal: Through all his offices, though his austerity was not different from the common run, his household had no stores; with kin, old friends, and former associates he even shared clothing and food, and never used a princely office for private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Across a long career he stayed as honest as any man yet kept no surplus; with friends and family he shared coat and bowl, and never traded on a royal appointment.

sentences.zh: 及卒，追贈太保，諡曰成。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously awarded grand guardian; his posthumous title was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously named grand guardian with the epithet Cheng, "Accomplished."

sentences.zh: 子贊嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 少子儉，字仲約，曆左積弩將軍、屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: His younger son Jian, courtesy name Zhongyue, successively held the posts of general of the left stacked crossbows and colonel of garrison cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: A younger son, Jian, courtesy name Zhongyue, served as general of the left stacked crossbows and colonel of garrison cavalry.

sentences.zh: 儉子弘，字世彥，少有清節，永嘉末，曆給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Jian's son Hong, courtesy name Shiyan, in youth had pure integrity; at the end of the Yongjia era he successively served as palace attendant for yellow gates and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Hong, courtesy name Shiyan, showed integrity early; late in Yongjia he held posts as palace attendant and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 劉寔，字子真，平原高唐人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shi, courtesy name Zizhen, was a man of Gaotang in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi, courtesy name Zizhen, came from Gaotang in Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢濟北惠王壽之後也，父廣，斥丘令。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Prince Hui of Jibei in Han; his father Guang was magistrate of Chiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He descended from Prince Hui of Jibei under the Han; his father Guang had been magistrate of Chiqiu.

sentences.zh: 寔少貧苦，賣牛衣以自給。

translations.literal: Shi in youth was poor and bitter; he sold cattle blankets to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up in deep poverty, patching his living by selling straw cattle-mats.

sentences.zh: 然好學，手約繩，口誦書，博通古今。

translations.literal: Yet he loved learning; with hand twining rope and mouth reciting texts, he became broadly conversant with ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: Still he studied obsessively, twisting rope as he walked and reciting texts until he commanded the whole tradition, past and present.

sentences.zh: 清身潔己，行無瑕玷。

translations.literal: He kept his person clear and himself pure; in conduct he had no blemish.
translations.idiomatic: He kept himself spotless; not a stain touched his name.

sentences.zh: 郡察孝廉，州舉秀才，皆不行。

translations.literal: The commandery investigated him as Filial and Incorrupt, the province nominated him as Flourishing Talent; in neither case did he go.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery nominated him Filial and Incorrupt, the province as Flourishing Talent; he accepted neither summons.

sentences.zh: 以計吏入洛，調為河南尹丞，遷尚書郎、廷尉正。

translations.literal: As accounts clerk he entered Luoyang, was transferred to be assistant to the governor of Henan, and was promoted to gentleman of the Masters of Writing and rectifier for the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Luoyang as a fiscal clerk, became aide to the Henan governor, then rose to gentleman of the Masters of Writing and rectifier at the commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 後曆吏部郎，參文帝相國軍事，封循陽子。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, joined Emperor Wen's (Sima Zhao) minister of state military staff, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to the Ministry of Personnel, served on Sima Zhao's minister-of-state staff, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 鐘會、鄧艾之伐蜀也，有客問寔曰：「二將其平蜀乎？

translations.literal: When Zhong Hui and Deng Ai campaigned against Shu, a guest asked Shi: "Will the two generals pacify Shu?"
translations.idiomatic: During Zhong Hui and Deng Ai's invasion of Shu, a visitor asked whether the two generals would conquer the west.

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「破蜀必矣，而皆不還。

translations.literal: Shi said: "They will surely break Shu, yet neither will return."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said Shu would fall, but neither commander would come back.

sentences.zh: 」客問其故，笑而不答，竟如其言。

translations.literal: The guest asked the reason; he smiled and did not answer, and in the end it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he smiled and held his tongue—and events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 寔之先見，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Shi's foresight was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His foresight was always of that order.

sentences.zh: 以世多進趣，廉遜道闕，乃著《崇讓論》以矯之。

translations.literal: Because the age favored rushing advancement and the way of integrity and yielding was lacking, he composed the "Treatise on Venerating Yielding" to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing a world mad for promotion and shy of modesty, he wrote his "Treatise on Venerating Yielding" to set it right.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its text says:
translations.idiomatic: It begins:

sentences.zh: 古之聖王之化天下，所以貴讓者，欲以出賢才，息爭競也。

translations.literal: The reason the sage kings of antiquity, in transforming the realm, honored yielding was that they wished thereby to bring forth worthy talent and still contention.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sage kings prized yielding because it drew talent forth and stilled strife.

sentences.zh: 夫人情莫不欲已之賢也，故勸令讓賢以自明賢也，豈假讓不賢哉！

translations.literal: As for human feeling, none does not wish himself worthy; therefore they urged one another to yield worthies in order to make clear their own worth—how could it be a false yielding of unworthiness!
translations.idiomatic: Every heart wants to seem worthy, so the wise urged men to yield place to the better—proving their own worth, not pretending virtue they lacked.

sentences.zh: 故讓道興，賢能之人不求而自出矣，至公之舉自立矣，百官之副亦豫具矣。

translations.literal: Therefore when the way of yielding flourishes, worthy and capable men emerge without being sought; the most impartial selections establish themselves; and the deputies for the hundred offices are also prepared in advance.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding is honored, talent steps forward unbidden, the fairest choices take care of themselves, and understudies for every post stand ready.

sentences.zh: 一官缺，擇眾官所讓最多者而用之，審之道也。

translations.literal: When one office is vacant, choose the one whom the host of officials has yielded to most often and employ him—this is the way of careful judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Fill a vacancy by promoting the man others most often stepped aside for—that is sound appointment.

sentences.zh: 在朝之士相讓於上，草廬之人咸皆化之，推賢讓能之風從此生矣。

translations.literal: Gentlemen at court yield to one another before their superiors; men in thatched huts are all transformed by it; the wind of recommending worthies and yielding to capability arises from this.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers defer to one another before the throne, rustics take the cue, and a culture of recommending the able begins.

sentences.zh: 為一國所讓，則一國士也；

translations.literal: He whom one state yields to is a gentleman of that state;
translations.idiomatic: The man a whole kingdom yields to is that kingdom's true gentleman;

sentences.zh: 天下所共推，則天下士也。

translations.literal: he whom the realm jointly recommends is a gentleman of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: the man the whole realm recommends is a gentleman of the realm.

sentences.zh: 推讓之風行，則賢與不肖灼然殊矣。

translations.literal: When the wind of recommendation and yielding prevails, worthy and unworthy stand clearly apart.
translations.idiomatic: Once yielding spreads, worthy men and fools are plain to tell apart.

sentences.zh: 此道之行，在上者無所用其心，因成清議，隨之而已。

translations.literal: When this way is practiced, those above need apply no artifice of mind; pure reputations form of themselves, and they need only follow along.
translations.idiomatic: Under that dispensation rulers need not scheme: clear public opinion forms, and they have only to follow it.

sentences.zh: 故曰，蕩蕩乎堯之為君，莫之能名。

translations.literal: Hence it is said, 'Vast was Yao as lord—none could name his art.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: Yao ruled so effortlessly that no one could describe how he did it.

sentences.zh: 言天下自安矣，不見堯所以化之，故不能名也。

translations.literal: It means the realm was at peace of itself; they did not see by what Yao transformed it, and therefore could not name it.
translations.idiomatic: The empire rested easy; people never saw his method, so they could not name it.

sentences.zh: 又曰，舜禹之有天下而不與焉，無為而化者其舜也歟。

translations.literal: It is also said, Shun and Yu had the realm yet seemed not to partake of it; he who transformed without acting was perhaps Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Again: Shun and Yu held the realm as if it were not theirs; Shun, perhaps, ruled by doing nothing yet changing everything.

sentences.zh: 賢人相讓于朝，大才之人恆在大官，小人不爭於野，天下無事矣。

translations.literal: Worthies yield to one another at court; men of great talent always hold high office; petty men do not contend in the wilds; the realm is without trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Worthies defer in the hall, great talent fills high posts, small men do not squabble in the fields, and the realm is calm.

sentences.zh: 以賢才化無事，至道興矣。

translations.literal: By worthy talent transforming into non-action, the highest way flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: When worthies shape a world that needs no meddling, the supreme Way prevails.

sentences.zh: 已仰其成，復何與焉！

translations.literal: Already looking up to its accomplishment—what further part is there to take!
translations.idiomatic: The ruler has only to trust the outcome—what is left to do?

sentences.zh: 故可以歌《南風》之詩，彈五弦之琴也。

translations.literal: Therefore one may sing the ode 'South Wind' and strum the five-stringed zither.
translations.idiomatic: Then he may sing the "South Wind" and strum the five-string lute in peace.

sentences.zh: 成此功者非有他，崇讓之所致耳。

translations.literal: That this achievement is brought about is due to nothing else but venerating yielding.
translations.idiomatic: None of this comes from anything but honoring yielding.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰，能以禮讓為國，則不難也。

translations.literal: Confucius said, 'If one can use ritual yielding to govern a state, it is not difficult.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said ruling a state through courteous yielding should not be hard.

sentences.zh: 在朝之人不務相讓久矣，天下化之。

translations.literal: The men at court have long not made it their business to yield to one another; the realm has been transformed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers have ceased deferring to one another, and the whole realm has taken the habit.

sentences.zh: 自魏代以來，登進辟命之士，及在職之吏，臨見受敘，雖自辭不能，終莫肯讓有勝己者。

translations.literal: From the Wei era onward, gentlemen advanced by summons and appointment, and officials in post, when they face audience and receive their order of rank, though they may decline claiming inability, in the end none is willing to yield to one who surpasses himself.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei, appointees and serving clerks—however they may protest incompetence at audience—refuse to step aside for anyone better.

sentences.zh: 夫推讓之風息，爭競之心生。

translations.literal: When the wind of yielding dies, the heart of contention is born.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding dies, rivalry is born.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰，上興讓則下不爭，明讓不興下必爭也。

translations.literal: Confucius said, 'When those above promote yielding, those below do not contend'—which shows that if yielding is not fostered above, those below will surely contend.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said when superiors honor yielding, inferiors do not fight—so if yielding is not fostered at the top, strife follows below.

sentences.zh: 推讓之道興，則賢能之人日見推舉；

translations.literal: When the way of yielding flourishes, worthy and capable men are daily seen recommended;
translations.idiomatic: Where yielding thrives, the able are lifted up each day;

sentences.zh: 爭競之心生，則賢能之人日見謗毀。

translations.literal: when the heart of contention is born, worthy and capable men are daily seen slandered and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: where rivalry rules, the able are torn down every day.

sentences.zh: 夫爭者之欲自先，甚惡能者之先，不能無毀也。

translations.literal: For the contender's desire to be first himself makes him deeply hate those able to be first; he cannot but destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Schemers must be first and hate anyone ahead of them; slander follows.

sentences.zh: 故孔墨不能免世之謗己，況不及孔墨者乎！

translations.literal: Therefore even Confucius and Mozi could not escape the age's slander against them—how much less those who do not match Confucius and Mozi!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius and Mozi could not escape slander—what hope for lesser men?

sentences.zh: 議者僉然言，世少高名之才，朝廷不有大才之人可以為大官者。

translations.literal: Discussants all say alike that the age lacks men of lofty reputation and the court has no men of great talent who could fill high office.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone laments a shortage of famous talent and claims no one at court is fit for the highest posts.

sentences.zh: 山澤人小官吏亦復雲，朝廷之士雖有大官名德，皆不及往時人也。

translations.literal: Petty clerks from mountain and marsh likewise say that although court gentlemen have high office and famed virtue, none matches men of former times.
translations.idiomatic: Even lowly clerks say today's grandees, however titled, cannot match the old stock.

sentences.zh: 餘以為此二言皆失之矣。

translations.literal: I consider that both these sayings miss the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Both verdicts, I believe, are wrong.

sentences.zh: 非時獨乏賢也，時不貴讓。

translations.literal: It is not that the age alone lacks worthies; the age does not honor yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The problem is not missing worthies but a climate that scorns yielding.

sentences.zh: 一人有先眾之譽，毀必隨之，名不得成使之然也。

translations.literal: When one man has a reputation ahead of the crowd, destruction surely follows him; his name cannot be completed—this makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: Outshine the pack and attack dogs follow; reputations never mature—that is why.

sentences.zh: 雖令稷契復存，亦不復能全其名矣。

translations.literal: Even if Ji and Xie were restored to life, they could no longer preserve their good names intact.
translations.idiomatic: Even Ji and Xie reborn could not keep their names whole.

sentences.zh: 能否混雜，優劣不分，士無素定之價，官職有缺，主選之吏不知所用，但案官次而舉之。

translations.literal: Able and unable are mixed together, excellence and inferiority undistinguished; gentlemen have no settled standing; when offices are vacant, the clerks in charge of selection do not know whom to use, but only go by order of rank and raise them.
translations.idiomatic: Able and useless blur together, no fixed scale judges men, and when a post opens selectors fall back on seniority because they cannot tell talent from rot.

sentences.zh: 同才之人先用者，非勢家之子，則必為有勢者之所念也。

translations.literal: Among men of like talent, the one first employed is either a son of a powerful house or must be one favored by the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Among equals, the first picked is always a magnate's son or a favorite of magnates.

sentences.zh: 非能獨賢，因其先用之資，而復遷之無已。

translations.literal: It is not that he alone is worthy; because of the capital of being first employed, he is promoted again without end.
translations.idiomatic: Not because he alone excels—early promotion becomes a ladder without end.

sentences.zh: 遷之無已，不勝其任之病發矣。

translations.literal: Promoted without end, the malady of being unequal to one's charge breaks out.
translations.idiomatic: Endless promotion soon exposes men who cannot bear the load.

sentences.zh: 觀在官之人，政績無聞，自非勢家之子，率多因資次而進也。

translations.literal: Observe the men in office: administrative achievement goes unremarked; unless they are sons of powerful houses, for the most part they have advanced by seniority of credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Look at serving officials—few distinguished records; unless born to power, most rose by stacking years.

sentences.zh: 向令天下貴讓，士必由於見讓而後名成，名成而官乃得用之。

translations.literal: Suppose the realm honored yielding: gentlemen would have to achieve reputation through being yielded to, and only when reputation was formed could offices employ them.
translations.idiomatic: If yielding were prized, a man would earn his name only after others stepped aside for him, and only then would office follow.

sentences.zh: 諸名行不立之人，在官無政績之稱，讓之者必矣，官無因得而用之也。

translations.literal: As for those whose reputations and conduct do not stand, who in office have no praise for administrative achievement—yielding to them would be certain, and offices would have no occasion to employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Men without standing or record would find others yielding their turn, and government would have no cause to use them.

sentences.zh: 所以見用不息者，由讓道廢，因資用人之有失久矣。

translations.literal: The reason they are employed without cease is that the way of yielding has been abandoned and the error of going by seniority in employing men has long persisted.
translations.idiomatic: They keep their posts because yielding died out and seniority-based appointment has gone uncorrected for ages.

sentences.zh: 故自漢魏以來，時開大舉，令眾官各舉所知，唯才所任，不限階次，如此者甚數矣。

translations.literal: Therefore from Han and Wei onward, there have often been great call-ups ordering the host of officials each to recommend those he knew, appointing solely by talent without limiting rank order—such instances have been very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei, repeated edicts told every official to nominate talent without regard to rank—again and again.

sentences.zh: 其所舉必有當者，不聞時有擢用，不知何誰最賢故也。

translations.literal: Among those recommended there must be suitable men, yet one does not hear of timely promotions—because no one knows who is most worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Some nominees must be fit, yet none are heard of being raised—no one can tell who is best.

sentences.zh: 所舉必有不當，而罪不加，不知何誰最不肖也。

translations.literal: Among those recommended there must be unsuitable men, yet punishment is not applied—because no one knows who is most unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Some must be unfit, yet no one is punished—no one can pick out the worst.

sentences.zh: 所以不可得知，由當時之人莫肯相推，賢愚之名不別，令其如此。

translations.literal: The reason it cannot be known is that people of the time are unwilling to defer to one another; the names of worthy and foolish are not distinguished, which makes it thus.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is simple: no one defers, worthy and fool look the same, so judgment collapses.

sentences.zh: 舉者知在上者察不能審，故敢漫舉而進之。

translations.literal: The recommenders know those above cannot investigate with care, and therefore dare to recommend carelessly and advance them.
translations.idiomatic: Nominators know superiors cannot vet closely, so they toss names forward at random.

sentences.zh: 或舉所賢，因及所念，一頓而至，人數猥多，各言所舉者賢，加之高狀，相似如一，難得而分矣。

translations.literal: Some recommend those they esteem, extending to those they favor; in one batch the names arrive, the crowd is vast, each declares his nominee worthy, adds lofty characterizations—all alike—and they are hard to separate.
translations.idiomatic: Some push favorites and hangers-on in a single flood; every file swears its man is brilliant, the praise reads the same, and no one can sort them.

sentences.zh: 參錯相亂，真偽同貫，更復由此而甚。

translations.literal: They tangle and confuse one another; true and false share one thread, and from this it becomes still worse.
translations.idiomatic: Truth and humbug tangle until the mess grows worse.

sentences.zh: 雖舉者不能盡忠之罪，亦由上開聽察之路濫，令其爾也。

translations.literal: Though there is also the fault of recommenders not being fully loyal, it is because those above opened a path of listening and inspection that is excessive, which makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: Recommenders share the blame, but the throne invited the abuse by listening too wide.

sentences.zh: 昔齊王好聽竽聲，必令三百人合吹而後聽之，廩以數人之俸。

translations.literal: Formerly the king of Qi loved to hear the yu pipes and always had three hundred men blow together before he would listen, paying them stipends at the rate of several men each.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi insisted on three hundred yu players at once and paid each as several common musicians.

sentences.zh: 南郭先生不知吹竽者也，以三百人合吹可以容其不知，因請為王吹竽，虛食數人之俸。

translations.literal: Master Nanguo did not know how to play the yu; because three hundred blowing together could hide his ignorance, he asked to play for the king and ate idle pay worth several men's salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Mr. Nanguo could not play, but the massed band hid him; he drew several musicians' pay for nothing.

sentences.zh: 嗣王覺而改之，難彰先王之過。

translations.literal: The succeeding king perceived it and changed the practice, yet found it hard to expose the former king's fault.
translations.idiomatic: The next king saw the fraud but hesitated to shame his father.

sentences.zh: 乃下令曰：「吾之好聞竽聲有甚于先王，欲一一列而聽之。

translations.literal: He therefore issued an order: "My love of hearing the yu is even greater than the former king's; I wish to have them arrayed one by one and listen to each."
translations.idiomatic: He decreed, "I love the yu more than my father—bring the players forward one at a time."

sentences.zh: 」先生于此逃矣。

translations.literal: At this the master fled.
translations.idiomatic: Nanguo ran.

sentences.zh: 推賢之風不立，濫舉之法不改，則南郭先生之徒盈於朝矣。

translations.literal: If the wind of recommending worthies is not established and the law of reckless recommendation is not reformed, then disciples of Master Nanguo will fill the court.
translations.idiomatic: Without real recommendation and reform, the court fills with Nanguos.

sentences.zh: 才高守道之士日退，馳走有勢之門日多矣。

translations.literal: Men of high talent who keep the Way daily withdraw; those who gallop to the gates of the powerful daily grow more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: True talent retreats while careerists crowd the mighty.

sentences.zh: 雖國有典刑，弗能禁矣。

translations.literal: Though the state has statutes and punishments, it cannot stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes alone cannot stop it.

sentences.zh: 夫讓道不興之弊，非徒賢人在下位，不得時進也，國之良臣荷重任者，亦將以漸受罪退矣。

translations.literal: The harm when the way of yielding does not flourish is not only that worthies in low posts cannot advance in time; the state's good ministers who bear heavy responsibility will also by degrees suffer punishment and removal.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding fails, not only do the worthy stall below—even trusted ministers fall, step by step, to disgrace.

sentences.zh: 何以知其然也？

translations.literal: How do we know it is so?
translations.idiomatic: How do we know?

sentences.zh: 孔子以為顏氏之子不貳過耳，明非聖人皆有過。

translations.literal: Confucius thought that only the son of the Yan clan did not repeat a fault—which makes clear that even non-sages all have faults.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said only Yan Hui never repeated a mistake—so everyone short of a sage errs.

sentences.zh: 寵貴之地欲之者多矣，惡賢能者塞其路，其過而毀之者亦多矣。

translations.literal: The places of favor and eminence are much desired; those who hate the worthy and able block their path, and those who seize their faults to destroy them are also many.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone covets high place; rivals block the able and pounce on every slip.

sentences.zh: 夫謗毀之生，非徒空設，必因人之微過而甚之者也。

translations.literal: The birth of slander and ruin is not mere empty invention; it must amplify someone's small fault.
translations.idiomatic: Slander never comes from nowhere—it magnifies a speck into a stain.

sentences.zh: 譭謗之言數聞，在上者雖欲弗納，不能不杖所聞，因事之來而微察之也，無以，其驗至矣。

translations.literal: When words of vilification are repeatedly heard, though those above may wish not to accept them, they cannot but rely on what they have heard; when matters arise they investigate subtly—and when nothing avails, the proof arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors pile up; rulers may wish to ignore them yet must act on what they hear, probing each case until the evidence lands.

sentences.zh: 得其驗，安得不理其罪。

translations.literal: When the proof is obtained, how can one fail to deal with the crime?
translations.idiomatic: Proof in hand, punishment follows.

sentences.zh: 若知而縱之，王之威日衰，令之不行自此始矣。

translations.literal: If one knows yet indulges it, the king's majesty daily wanes; orders not being obeyed begin from this.
translations.idiomatic: To know and wink at it drains royal authority and orders cease to run.

sentences.zh: 知而皆理之，受罪退者稍多，大臣有不自固之心。

translations.literal: If one knows and deals with them all, those who suffer punishment and removal gradually grow more numerous, and great ministers have hearts no longer secure in themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Punish every case and dismissed ministers multiply; the great officers lose their footing.

sentences.zh: 夫賢才不進，貴臣日疏，此有國者之深憂也。

translations.literal: When worthy talent does not advance and honored ministers daily grow distant, this is the deep worry of one who holds a state.
translations.idiomatic: Talent blocked and pillars estranged—any ruler's nightmare.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「受祿不讓，至於已斯亡。

translations.literal: The Book of Songs says: "Receiving emolument without yielding—when it reaches oneself, thus one perishes."
translations.idiomatic: The Songs warn: grasp pay without yielding and ruin follows.

sentences.zh: 」不讓之人憂亡不暇，而望其益國朝，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Men who do not yield have no leisure from worry over ruin—yet to expect them to benefit the court-state—is it not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Men who never yield busy themselves with survival—can they serve the dynasty?

sentences.zh: 竊以為改此俗甚易耳。

translations.literal: I privately consider changing this custom very easy.
translations.idiomatic: I believe this habit could be broken with ease.

sentences.zh: 何以知之？

translations.literal: How do I know it?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 夫一時在官之人，雖雜有凡猥之才，其中賢明者亦多矣，豈可謂皆不知讓賢為貴邪！

translations.literal: Among the men in office at any one time, though they are mixed with talent that is ordinary and base, among them the worthy and enlightened are also many—how can one say they all do not know that yielding to worthies is precious!
translations.idiomatic: Officialdom always mixes mediocrities with many bright men—they know yielding matters.

sentences.zh: 直以其時皆不讓，習以成俗，故遂不為耳。

translations.literal: It is simply that at that time none yielded; habit formed custom, and therefore they finally did not do it.
translations.idiomatic: Habit alone stops them—no one yields, so no one yields.

sentences.zh: 人臣初除，皆通表上聞，名之謝章，所由來尚矣。

translations.literal: When ministers are first appointed, they all send in memorials to inform above; these are called thanks memorials—their origin is long-standing.
translations.idiomatic: New appointees always submit a memorial of thanks—an old rite.

sentences.zh: 原謝章之本意，欲進賢能以謝國恩也。

translations.literal: Tracing the original intent of the thanks memorial, it was to advance worthy talent in order to thank the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: The point was to recommend better men while thanking the throne.

sentences.zh: 昔舜以禹為司空，禹拜稽首，讓於稷契及咎繇。

translations.literal: Formerly Shun made Yu minister of works; Yu bowed his head to the ground and yielded to Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Shun named Yu minister of works; Yu kowtowed and ceded to Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao.

sentences.zh: 使益為虞官，讓於硃虎、熊、羆。

translations.literal: He appointed Yi forest and marsh officer; he yielded to Zhu Hu, Xiong, and Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was set over forests and marshes and yielded to Zhu Hu, Xiong, and Pi.

sentences.zh: 使伯夷典三禮，讓于夔龍。

translations.literal: He appointed Boyi to oversee the three rites; he yielded to Kui and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Boyi took the three rites and deferred to Kui and Long.

sentences.zh: 唐虞之時，眾官初除，莫不皆讓也。

translations.literal: In the time of Tang and Yu, when the host of officials were first appointed, none failed to yield.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yao and Shun every new officer yielded.

sentences.zh: 謝章之義，蓋取於此。

translations.literal: The meaning of the thanks memorial is drawn from this.
translations.idiomatic: The thanks memorial comes from that spirit.

sentences.zh: 《書》記之者，欲以永世作則。

translations.literal: The Document records them in order to make a model for all ages.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic records it as a pattern for all time.

sentences.zh: 季世所用，不賢不能讓賢，虛謝見用之恩而已。

translations.literal: What declining ages use: if one is not worthy one cannot yield to worthies; they vainly thank the grace of being employed—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages hollowed it out—unworthy men cannot yield, so they mouth thanks and mean nothing.

sentences.zh: 相承不變，習俗之失也。

translations.literal: Handed down unchanged—it is the error of habit and custom.
translations.idiomatic: Custom froze, and the rite rotted.

sentences.zh: 夫敘用之官得通章表者，其讓賢推能乃通，其不能有所讓徒費簡紙者，皆絕不通。

translations.literal: Among appointment officials who may submit memorials, only if they yield to worthies and recommend capability should it pass through; those who cannot yield anything but vainly waste bamboo and paper—all cut off, not passed through.
translations.idiomatic: Let every appointing officer who may memorialize do so only to recommend a better man; empty thanks waste paper and go nowhere.

sentences.zh: 人臣初除，各思推賢能而讓之矣，讓之文付主者掌之。

translations.literal: When ministers are first appointed, let each think to recommend worthy talent and yield to it; the documents of yielding are to be handed to the presiding official to keep.
translations.idiomatic: At each new posting, men should nominate superiors and defer; those writings go to the registrar.

sentences.zh: 三司有缺，擇三司所讓最多者而用之。

translations.literal: When one of the Three Dukes is vacant, choose the one whom the Three Dukes have yielded to most often and employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Fill a Three Duke vacancy from the man the three most often stepped aside for.

sentences.zh: 此為一公缺，三公已豫選之矣。

translations.literal: This means one duke is vacant, yet the Three Dukes have already preselected him.
translations.idiomatic: One seat opens, but the three have already picked his successor.

sentences.zh: 且主選之吏，不必任公而選三公，不如令三公自共選一公為詳也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the clerks in charge of selection need not be given a duke's post in order to select the Three Dukes—it is better to order the Three Dukes jointly to select one duke, which is more thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Selectors need not be dukes themselves; better the Three Dukes jointly pick the third—that is sounder.

sentences.zh: 四征缺，擇四征所讓最多而用之，此為一征缺，四征已豫選之矣，必詳於停缺而令主者選四征也。

translations.literal: When one of the four expeditions is vacant, choose the one whom the four expeditions have yielded to most and employ him—this means one expedition is vacant, yet the four have already preselected him; it is surely more thorough than leaving the post vacant and ordering the presiding official to select among the four expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: One expeditionary post empty? The four generals have already ranked their choices—far better than leaving the job open while a clerk picks among them.

sentences.zh: 尚書缺，擇尚書所讓最多者而用之，此為八尚書共選一尚書，詳于臨缺令主者選八尚書也。

translations.literal: When a Masters of Writing post is vacant, choose the one whom the Masters of Writing have yielded to most and employ him—this means the eight Masters of Writing jointly select one Master of Writing, which is more thorough than facing a vacancy and ordering the presiding official to select among eight Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: For a Masters of Writing seat, let the eight ministers jointly elevate the colleague most deferred to—better than a hurried search when the chair is empty.

sentences.zh: 郡守缺，擇眾郡所讓最多者而用之，詳于任主者令選百郡守也。

translations.literal: When a commandery governor is vacant, choose the one whom the host of commanderies have yielded to most and employ him; this is more thorough than entrusting the presiding official to select among a hundred commandery governors.
translations.idiomatic: Governors should be the man the commanderies most often yielded to—not a central clerk paging through a hundred names.

sentences.zh: 夫以眾官百郡之讓，與主者共相比，不可同歲而論也。

translations.literal: To compare the yielding of the host of officials and hundred commanderies with that of the presiding official together—they cannot be spoken of in the same breath.
translations.idiomatic: Collective yielding from every office and commandery dwarfs what one appointing clerk can know.

sentences.zh: 雖復令三府參舉官，本不委以舉選之任，各不能以根其心也。

translations.literal: Even if one orders the three bureaus to participate in recommending officials, fundamentally they are not entrusted with the duty of recommendation and selection, and each cannot get to the root in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the three bureaus "help" nominate, they lack real selection power and never invest their hearts in it.

sentences.zh: 其所用心者裁之不二三，但令主者案官次而舉之，不用精也。

translations.literal: What they apply their minds to trims no more than two or three; they only order the presiding official to go by order of rank and raise them—not employing care.
translations.idiomatic: They skim two or three names and tell the clerk to follow seniority—no real thought.

sentences.zh: 賢愚皆讓，百姓耳目盡為國耳目。

translations.literal: Worthy and foolish alike yield; the ears and eyes of the hundred surnames all become the state's ears and eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When everyone defers, the people become the ruler's eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 夫人情爭則欲毀己所不知，讓則競推於勝己。

translations.literal: As for human feeling: when they contend they wish to destroy what they do not know; when they yield they compete to push forward those who surpass themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Rivalry breeds slander of the unknown; yielding lifts the better man.

sentences.zh: 故世爭則毀譽交錯，優劣不分，難得而讓也。

translations.literal: Therefore when the age contends, slander and praise tangle; excellence and inferiority are not distinguished, and yielding is hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: In a contentious age praise and blame tangle and no one yields.

sentences.zh: 時讓則賢智顯出，能否之美歷歷相次，不可得而亂也。

translations.literal: When the age yields, the worthy and wise stand forth; the beauty of capability and incapability stands out in clear sequence and cannot be confused.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding rules, talent shines and competence sorts itself unmistakably.

sentences.zh: 當此時也，能退身修已者，讓之者多矣。

translations.literal: At such a time, those who can withdraw and cultivate themselves will have many who yield to them.
translations.idiomatic: Then men who step back and refine themselves win the most deferrals.

sentences.zh: 雖欲守貧賤，不可得也。

translations.literal: Though they may wish to keep to poverty and lowliness, they cannot obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot stay poor and obscure if they try.

sentences.zh: 馳騖進趣而欲人見讓，猶卻行而求前也。

translations.literal: To gallop after advancement and yet wish others to yield to you is like walking backward to seek forward progress.
translations.idiomatic: Scrambling for promotion while expecting deference is walking backward and calling it forward.
