sentences.zh: 夫如此，愚智咸知進身求通，非修之於己則無由矣。

translations.literal: If it is thus, foolish and wise alike know that to advance the person and seek success there is no way unless they cultivate it in themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Then fool and sage alike see that advancement rides on self-cultivation, not intrigue.

sentences.zh: 游外求者，於此相隨而歸矣。

translations.literal: Those who roam outside seeking will hereupon follow along and return.
translations.idiomatic: Adventurers hunting outside favor come home to inward work.

sentences.zh: 浮聲虛論，不禁而自息矣。

translations.literal: Floating reputations and empty discourse, without being forbidden, cease of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hollow fame dies without a ban.

sentences.zh: 人人無所用其心，任眾人之議，而天下自化矣。

translations.literal: Each person has no need to apply his mind; trusting the multitude's judgment, the realm transforms itself.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers need not scheme—trust public judgment and the realm rights itself.

sentences.zh: 不言之化行，巍巍之美於此著矣。

translations.literal: Transformation without words is practiced; the beauty of majesty hereby stands forth.
translations.idiomatic: Silent transformation unfolds and true majesty appears.

sentences.zh: 讓可以致此，豈可不務之哉！

translations.literal: Yielding can bring this about—how can one fail to pursue it!
translations.idiomatic: Yielding achieves this—how can we neglect it?

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：「范宣子之讓，其下皆讓。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn says: "When Fan Xuanzi yielded, those below him all yielded."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo says when Fan Xuanzi stepped aside, his subordinates did the same.

sentences.zh: 欒黶雖汰，弗敢違也。

translations.literal: Though Luan Yan was arrogant, he did not dare disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Even arrogant Luan Yan dared not refuse.

sentences.zh: 晉國以平，數世賴之。

translations.literal: Jin thereby was pacified; for several generations it relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Jin grew calm and prospered for generations on that habit.

sentences.zh: 」上世之化也，君子尚能而讓其下，小人力農以事其上，上下有禮，讒慝遠黜，由不爭也。

translations.literal: Such was the transformation of high antiquity: gentlemen esteemed capability and yielded to those below; petty men labored in agriculture to serve those above; above and below had ritual propriety; slander and wickedness were banished far off—because there was no contention.
translations.idiomatic: That was high antiquity: the great deferred to subordinates, farmers served their betters, ritual ran top to bottom, and slander fled—because no one fought rank.

sentences.zh: 及其亂也，國家之弊，恆必由之。

translations.literal: When it came to their disorder, the ills of state always arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: When order broke, state's ills always traced to losing that.

sentences.zh: 篤論了了如此。

translations.literal: The firm judgment is clear thus.
translations.idiomatic: The moral is plain.

sentences.zh: 在朝君子典選大官，能不以人廢言，舉而行之，各以讓賢舉能為先務，則群才猥出，能否殊別，蓋世之功，莫大於此。

translations.literal: If gentlemen at court who oversee selection and great offices can, without discarding words because of the person, raise and practice this, each taking yielding to worthies and raising capability as the first task, then a host of talents will pour forth, capability and incapability will be clearly distinguished, and for an age-covering achievement nothing is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: If high selectors heed this essay and put yielding first, talent will flood forth, competence will sort itself, and no policy could do more for an age.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，進爵為伯，累遷少府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taishi era he was advanced in noble rank to earl and was promoted in stages to minister of the lesser treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he was raised to earl and rose through the ministry of the lesser treasury.

sentences.zh: 咸甯中為太常。

translations.literal: During the Xianning era he became chamberlain for ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianning he served as chamberlain for ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 杜預之伐吳也，寔以本官行鎮南軍司。

translations.literal: When Du Yu campaigned against Wu, Shi, in his current office, acted as army director for the general who guards the south.
translations.idiomatic: During Du Yu's conquest of Wu he served as army director on the southern command staff in his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 初，寔妻盧氏生子躋而卒，華氏將以女妻之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shi's wife the Lady Lu bore a son, Ji, then died; the Hua clan was about to give him a daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: His first wife, Lady Lu, bore a son, Ji, then died; the Huas offered him a daughter.

sentences.zh: 寔弟智諫曰：「華家類貪，必破門戶。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Zhi remonstrated: "The Hua clan is characteristically grasping—they will surely ruin the household."
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhi warned, "The Huas are a grasping clan—they will break our house."

sentences.zh: 」辭之不得，竟婚華氏而生子夏。

translations.literal: He could not decline; in the end he married the Hua daughter and she bore a son, Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He could not refuse; he wed the Hua woman and she bore Xia.

sentences.zh: 寔竟坐夏受賂，免官。

translations.literal: Shi was convicted because Xia accepted bribes and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xia's bribery cost Shi his post.

sentences.zh: 頃之為大司農，又以夏罪免。

translations.literal: Before long he became minister of agriculture, then again was removed on account of Xia's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was minister of agriculture, then lost that office too over Xia's crimes.

sentences.zh: 寔每還州裏，鄉人載酒肉以候之。

translations.literal: Whenever Shi returned to his home commandery, fellow villagers brought wine and meat to wait for him.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he came home, neighbors met him with wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 寔難逆其意，輒共啖而返其餘。

translations.literal: Shi found it hard to go against their intent; he would always eat with them and return the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to refuse their kindness, he shared the meal and sent the leftovers back.

sentences.zh: 或謂寔曰：「君行高一世，而諸子不能遵。

translations.literal: Someone said to Shi: "Your conduct towers above the age, yet your sons cannot follow it."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told him, "Your virtue outshines the age, yet your sons do not follow it."

sentences.zh: 何不旦夕切磋，使知過而自改邪！

translations.literal: Why not day and night grind and polish them, so that they know their faults and reform themselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not coach them morning and night until they mend their ways?"

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「吾之所行，是所聞見，不相祖習，豈復教誨之所得乎！

translations.literal: Shi said: "What I practice is what I have heard and seen; we do not mutually inherit habit—how could it come from instruction and teaching!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi answered, "What I do I learned by sight and sound, not by rote from elders—lectures will not graft that onto my sons."

sentences.zh: 」世以寔言為當。

translations.literal: The age considered Shi's words apt.
translations.idiomatic: People judged him right.

sentences.zh: 後起為國子祭酒、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later he was raised to libationer of the imperial academy and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as libationer of the national university and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子初封廣陵王，高選師友，以寔為師。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai was first enfeoffed as prince of Guangling, high selection was made of tutors and companions, and Shi was made his tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Minhuai was first prince of Guangling, the court chose eminent tutors; Shi became his teacher.

sentences.zh: 元康初，進爵為侯，累遷太子太保，加侍中、特進、右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，領冀州都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuankang era he was advanced in rank to marquis, was promoted in stages to junior tutor to the heir apparent, and was given the additional titles palace attendant, specially advanced, grand master of the right of splendid happiness, opener of office with ceremonial parity with the Three Dukes, and concurrent area commander for Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang he became a marquis, rose to junior tutor to the heir apparent, and accumulated palace attendant, Specially Advanced, grand master of the right, opener of office equal to the Three Dukes, and area command over Ji.

sentences.zh: 九年，策拜司空，遷太保，轉太傅。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was invested by patent as minister of works, promoted to grand tutor, and transferred to grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he received the minister of works patent, then grand tutor, then grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太安初，寔以老病遜位，賜安車駟馬、錢百萬，以侯就第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tai'an era Shi yielded his post on account of old age and illness; he was given a secure carriage, four horses, and a million cash, and as marquis retired to his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tai'an age and illness drove him to retire; the throne sent a carriage, four horses, a million cash, and let him close out his days as marquis at home.

sentences.zh: 及長沙成都之相攻也，寔為軍人所掠，潛歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When the princes of Changsha and Chengdu attacked each other, Shi was plundered by soldiers and secretly returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: When the princes of Changsha and Chengdu turned on each other, soldiers robbed him; he slipped home to the country.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔曰：「昔虞任五臣，致垂拱之化，漢相蕭何，興寧一之譽，故能光隆於當時，垂裕於百代。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict said: "Formerly Shun employed five ministers and achieved the transformation of folded hands on high; Han's chancellor Xiao He raised the renown of unity and rest—therefore they could shine and flourish in their age and leave abundance for a hundred generations."
translations.idiomatic: A third-year edict read: "Shun's five ministers brought effortless rule; Xiao He won Han fame for unity—so they glorified their times and left a legacy for ages."

sentences.zh: 朕紹天明命，臨御萬邦，所以崇顯政道者，亦賴之於元臣庶尹，畢力股肱，以副至望。

translations.literal: We inherit the bright mandate of Heaven and face the myriad regions; the means by which We elevate and display the way of government likewise rely on chief ministers and many directors, exhausting their strength as arms and legs, to match utmost expectation."
translations.idiomatic: We hold Heaven's mandate over the realm; good government rests on pillar ministers giving their all as Our arms and legs."

sentences.zh: 而君年耆告老，確然難違。

translations.literal: Yet you, lord, are advanced in years and have announced retirement—firmly, and hard to gainsay.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are old and ask to retire—your resolve brooks no refusal.

sentences.zh: 今聽君以侯就第，位居三司之上，秩祿准舊，賜几杖不朝及宅一區。

translations.literal: Now We accede to your retiring to your mansion as marquis, with position above the Three Dukes, salary and emoluments as before, and We grant staff and cushion exemption from court attendance and one residence.
translations.idiomatic: We grant your wish to close out life as marquis at home, rank above the Three Dukes, salary unchanged, with staff-and-cushion privilege, exemption from court, and a house.

sentences.zh: 國之大政，將就諮於君，副朕意焉。

translations.literal: Great policies of state We shall come to consult with you, to match Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: On weighty affairs We will still seek your counsel—such is Our mind."

sentences.zh: 」歲余薨，時年九十一，諡曰元。

translations.literal: After a little over a year he died, aged ninety-one; his posthumous title was Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died at ninety-one with the posthumous name Yuan, "Primordial."

sentences.zh: 寔少貧窶，杖策徒行，每所憩止，不累主人，薪水之事，皆自營給。

translations.literal: Shi in youth was poor and shabby; staff in hand he went on foot; wherever he rested he did not burden his host; firewood and water he always supplied himself.
translations.idiomatic: Youth left him threadbare; he walked with a stick, imposed on no host for fuel or water, and saw to his own needs.

sentences.zh: 及位望通顯，每崇儉素，不尚華麗。

translations.literal: When his position and renown were eminent, he always honored austerity and plainness and did not esteem splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Even when powerful and famous he clung to plain living and scorned display.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣石崇家，如廁，見有絳紋帳，裀褥甚麗，兩婢持香囊。

translations.literal: He once called on Shi Chong's house and went to the privy; he saw a crimson-patterned canopy, very fine mats and bedding, and two maids holding sachets.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Shi Chong, he stepped into a lavatory hung with crimson silk, rich cushions, and two maids bearing perfume bags.

sentences.zh: 寔便退，笑謂崇曰：「誤入卿內。

translations.literal: Shi drew back and said with a smile to Chong: "I mistakenly entered your inner chambers."
translations.idiomatic: He stepped back and laughed, "I have wandered into your private rooms by mistake."

sentences.zh: 」崇曰：「是廁耳。

translations.literal: Chong said: "It is only the privy."
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "That is only the toilet."

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「貧士未嘗得此。

translations.literal: Shi said: "A poor scholar has never had such a thing."
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, "A poor scholar never sees the like."

sentences.zh: 」乃更如他廁。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went instead to another privy.
translations.idiomatic: He used another lavatory instead.

sentences.zh: 雖處榮寵，居無第宅，所得俸祿，贍恤親故。

translations.literal: Though he stood in honor and favor, he had no mansion residence; what he received in salary and stipend he used to support kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Despite favor at court he owned no grand house and sent every salary to kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 雖禮教陵遲，而行己以正。

translations.literal: Though ritual instruction was in decline, in conducting himself he held to rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: While public morals slid, he kept his own conduct straight.

sentences.zh: 喪妻為廬杖之制，終喪不禦內。

translations.literal: Mourning his wife he observed the hut-and-staff rites and through the end of mourning did not enter the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: For his wife's death he built the mourning hut and carried the staff, and until mourning ended he did not visit the women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 輕薄者笑之，寔不以介意。

translations.literal: Frivolous men laughed at him; Shi did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wits mocked him; he ignored them.

sentences.zh: 自少及老，篤學不倦，雖居職務，卷弗離手。

translations.literal: From youth to old age he loved learning tirelessly; though he held office, a book never left his hand.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood to age he never tired of books; even in office he read constantly.

sentences.zh: 尤精《三傳》，辨正《公羊》，以為衛輒不應辭以王父命，祭仲失為臣之節，舉此二端以明臣子之體，遂行於世。

translations.literal: He held that Duke Zhu of Wei's son Kua should not have refused on the order of his grandfather, and that Jizhong failed the integrity of a minister—raising these two points to clarify the body of minister-and-son duty, which thereupon circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Three Commentaries and challenged the Gongyang: Duke Zhu of Wei was wrong to cite his grandfather's command, and Jizhong of Zheng broke a minister's duty. Those two cases became his standard for subject and son, and his reading spread.

sentences.zh: 又撰《春秋條例》二十卷。

translations.literal: He also compiled twenty fascicles of "Spring and Autumn Regulations."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote twenty chapters of "Spring and Autumn Regulations."

sentences.zh: 有二子，躋、夏。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Ji and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Ji and Xia.

sentences.zh: 躋字景雲，官至散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Jingyun, rose in office to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, courtesy name Jingyun, reached the post of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 夏以貪污棄放於世。

translations.literal: Xia because of corruption was cast off and banished in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xia was ruined by greed and cast out of respectable society.

sentences.zh: 弟智，字子房，貞素有兄風。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhi, courtesy name Zifang, was chaste and plain and had his elder brother's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhi, courtesy name Zifang, was as upright and austere as his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 少貧窶，每負薪自給，讀誦不輟，竟以儒行稱。

translations.literal: In youth he was poor and shabby; he often carried firewood to support himself and did not cease reading and reciting; in the end he was praised for Confucian conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Poor in youth, he hauled firewood to live yet never stopped studying, and won fame as a Confucian gentleman.

sentences.zh: 曆中書黃門吏部郎，出為潁川太守。

translations.literal: He successively served as gentleman at the secretariat, yellow gates, and Ministry of Personnel, then went out as governor of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the secretariat, at yellow gates, and in the Ministry of Personnel, then became governor of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 平原管輅嘗謂人曰：「吾與劉潁川兄弟語，使人神思清發，昏不假寐。

translations.literal: Guan Lu of Pingyuan once said to someone: "When I converse with the Liu brothers of Yingchuan, it makes one's spirit and thoughts clear and quick; in the evening one needs no nap."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu of Pingyuan said, "Talking with the Liu brothers of Yingchuan clears the mind; you need no nap at dusk."

sentences.zh: 自此之外，殆白日欲寢矣。

translations.literal: Apart from this, one is almost ready to sleep in broad daylight."
translations.idiomatic: With anyone else I could nap in broad daylight."

sentences.zh: 」入為秘書監，領南陽王師，加散騎常侍，遷侍中、尚書、太常。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as director of the palace library, concurrent tutor to the prince of Nanyang, with additional appointment as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and was promoted to palace attendant, Masters of Writing, and chamberlain for ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director of the palace library and tutor to the prince of Nanyang, added as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, then rose to palace attendant, Masters of Writing, and chamberlain for ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 著《喪服釋疑論》，多所辨明。

translations.literal: He composed "Discourse Resolving Doubts on Mourning Dress" and clarified much.
translations.idiomatic: His "Discourse Resolving Doubts on Mourning Dress" settled many disputed points.

sentences.zh: 太康末卒，諡曰成。

translations.literal: He died at the end of the Taikang era; his posthumous title was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died late in Taikang with the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 高光，字宣茂，陳留圉城人，魏太尉柔之子也。

translations.literal: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, was a man of Yucheng in Chenliu, son of Grand Commandant Rou of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, came from Yucheng in Chenliu; he was the son of Wei grand commandant Gao Rou.

sentences.zh: 光少習家業，明練刑理。

translations.literal: Guang in youth studied the family occupation and was clear and practiced in penal principles.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in his father's legal tradition and mastered penal law.

sentences.zh: 初以太子舍人累遷尚書郎，出為幽州刺史、潁州太守。

translations.literal: First as household gentleman to the heir apparent he was promoted in stages to gentleman of the Masters of Writing, then went out as inspector of You Province and governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: From gentleman attendant on the heir apparent he rose to gentleman of the Masters of Writing, then served as inspector of You and governor of Ying commandery.

sentences.zh: 是時武帝置黃沙獄，以典詔囚。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu established the Yellow Sand prison to oversee imperial-order prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu then founded the Yellow Sand prison for edict cases.

sentences.zh: 以光曆世明法，用為黃沙御史，秩與中丞同，遷廷尉。

translations.literal: Because Guang through generations was clear in the law, he was appointed Yellow Sand palace secretary, with rank equal to the palace assistant secretary, and was promoted to commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: His family's legal expertise won him the Yellow Sand inspectorship, rank equal to the assistant secretary, then the commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 元康中，拜尚書，典三公曹。

translations.literal: During the Yuankang era he was appointed to the Masters of Writing and supervised the Three Dukes bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuankang he joined the Masters of Writing in charge of the Three Dukes section.

sentences.zh: 時趙王倫篡逆，光於其際，守道全貞。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao of Lun usurped in rebellion, Guang in that crisis kept the Way and preserved his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun seized the throne, Guang held to principle and kept his honor clean.

sentences.zh: 及倫賜死，齊王冏輔政，復以光為廷尉，遷尚書，加奉車都尉。

translations.literal: When Lun was ordered to die and Prince Qi of Jiong held the regency, Guang was again made commandant of justice, promoted to Masters of Writing, and given the additional title commandant of the imperial coach.
translations.idiomatic: After Lun's forced suicide and under Prince Jiong's regency he returned as commandant of justice, then Masters of Writing, with the title commandant of the imperial coach.

sentences.zh: 後從駕討成都王穎有勳，封延陵縣公，邑千八百戶。

translations.literal: Later he followed the imperial train in the campaign against Prince Chengdu of Ying and had merit; he was enfeoffed as duke of Yanling county with a fief of one thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against Prince Ying of Chengdu with distinction and received the duchy of Yanling, eighteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 于時朝廷咸推光明于用法，故頻典理官。

translations.literal: At that time the court all praised Guang as enlightened in applying the law; therefore he repeatedly superintended judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: The court deemed him a master of the law, so he kept judicial posts.

sentences.zh: 惠帝為張方所逼，幸長安，朝臣奔散，莫有從者，光獨侍帝而西。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui was pressed by Zhang Fang and went to Chang'an, court ministers fled and scattered; none accompanied the emperor, but Guang alone attended him westward.
translations.idiomatic: Forced west to Chang'an by Zhang Fang, Emperor Hui found every courtier had fled—only Guang stayed at his side.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left vice director of the Masters of Writing and given additional appointment as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He became left vice director of the Masters of Writing and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 光兄誕為上官巳等所用，曆徐、雍二州刺史。

translations.literal: Guang's elder brother Dan was employed by Shangguan Si and the rest and successively served as inspector of Xu and Yong provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Dan served Shangguan Si's faction and held the inspectorships of Xu and Yong.

sentences.zh: 誕性任放無倫次，而決烈過人，與光異操。

translations.literal: Dan by nature was unrestrained and without order, yet decisive and fierce beyond others, differing from Guang in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was wild and disorderly yet bold beyond most—a temper nothing like Guang's.

sentences.zh: 常謂光小節，恆輕侮之，光事誕愈謹。

translations.literal: He often called Guang petty in small points and constantly treated him with contempt; Guang served Dan all the more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: He sneered at Guang as fussy and slighted him; Guang only served him more dutifully.

sentences.zh: 帝既還洛陽，時太弟新立，重選傅訓，以光為少傅，加光祿大夫，常侍如故。

translations.literal: When the emperor had returned to Luoyang, at that time the imperial younger brother had newly been established; with emphasis tutors were reselected, and Guang was made junior tutor, given grand master of splendid happiness, and kept as attendant-in-ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Luoyang, with a new heir presumptive, the court re-picked tutors: Guang became junior tutor, grand master of splendid happiness, and kept his attendant post.

sentences.zh: 及懷帝即位，加光祿大夫金章紫綬，與傅祗並見推崇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended, Guang was given grand master of splendid happiness with gold seal and purple ribbon and, together with Fu Zhi, was alike esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai added the gold seal and purple ribbon to his splendid-happiness title; he and Fu Zhi stood equally honored.

sentences.zh: 尋為尚書令，本官如故。

translations.literal: Before long he became director of the Masters of Writing, his original offices remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was director of the Masters of Writing while keeping his other titles.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒，贈司空、侍中。

translations.literal: He died of illness and was posthumously awarded minister of works and palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness; the court posthumously named him minister of works and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 屬京洛傾覆，竟未加諡。

translations.literal: It fell in the time when the capital and Luoyang were overthrown; in the end no posthumous title was added.
translations.idiomatic: The fall of Luoyang left him without a posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 子韜字子遠，放佚無檢。

translations.literal: His son Tao, courtesy name Ziyuan, was dissolute and without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tao, courtesy name Ziyuan, was reckless and ungovernable.

sentences.zh: 光為廷尉時，韜受貨賕，有司奏案之，而光不知。

translations.literal: When Guang was commandant of justice, Tao accepted bribes; the relevant offices memorialized to investigate him, but Guang did not know.
translations.idiomatic: While Guang headed justice, Tao took bribes; the bureaus impeached him, yet Guang knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 時人雖非光不能防閑其子，以其用心有素，不以為累。

translations.literal: People of the time though they blamed Guang for not being able to fence in his son, because his intentions had long been pure, did not hold it against him.
translations.idiomatic: Critics faulted him for not controlling Tao, but his lifelong integrity spared him real blame.

sentences.zh: 初，光詣長安留台，以韜兼右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Guang went to the provisional administration at Chang'an, he made Tao concurrent general of the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang joined the Chang'an exiled court he gave Tao a concurrent post as general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 韜與殿省小人交通，及光卒，仍於喪中往來不絕。

translations.literal: Tao associated with petty men of the palace bureaus; when Guang died, he still went back and forth without cease even in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Tao consorted with palace underlings and, even during mourning for his father, kept up those visits.

sentences.zh: 時東海王越輔政，不朝觀。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Donghai of Yue held the regency and did not attend court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue of Donghai held power and skipped court.

sentences.zh: 韜知人心有望，密與太傅參軍薑賾、京兆杜概等謀討越，事泄伏誅。

translations.literal: Tao knew men's hearts had expectations; secretly with grand tutor staff adviser Jiang Ze, Du Gai of Jingzhao, and others he plotted to attack Yue; the affair leaked and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Reading popular resentment, Tao secretly joined Jiang Ze, Du Gai, and others to move against Yue; the plot leaked and he died on the block.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：下士競而文，中庸靜而質，不若進不足而退有餘也。

translations.literal: The historians say: lesser gentlemen strive and ornament; the middle course is still and plain—it is not as good as advancing insufficiently yet retreating with surplus.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: petty men chase polish; the balanced path is quiet and plain—better to fall short going forward than to lack room when stepping back.

sentences.zh: 魏舒、劉寔發慮精華，結綬登槐，覽止成務。

translations.literal: Wei Shu and Liu Shi brought forth the essence of reflection, tied their seals and ascended the locust terrace, viewed stopping and completed the task.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu and Liu Shi distilled deep judgment, took high office, and knew when to stop—finishing what they began.

sentences.zh: 季和切問近對，當官正色。

translations.literal: Jihe asked closely and answered near at hand; in office he was stern of mien.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi answered sharp questions plainly and held office with unbending dignity.

sentences.zh: 詩云「貪人敗類」，豈劉夏之謂歟！

translations.literal: The Songs say, 'The greedy man ruins his kind'—does it not mean Liu Xia!
translations.idiomatic: The Songs call the grasping man the ruin of his kind—was that not Liu Xia?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：舒言不矜，憙對千乘。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Shu was not boastful in speech; Xi answered a lord of a thousand chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Wei Shu spoke without swagger; Li Xi faced a prince regnant with plain truth.

sentences.zh: 子真、宣茂，雅志難陵。

translations.literal: Zizhen and Xuanmao—refined resolve hard to overtop.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi and Gao Guang—purposes too high to be trampled.

sentences.zh: 進忠能舉，退讓攸興。

translations.literal: Advancing loyalty, able to raise; in retiring, yielding thereby flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced loyalty and lifted the able; in yielding office they set the tone.

sentences.zh: 皎皎瑚器，來光玉繩。

translations.literal: Bright, bright vessels of coral; they bring light to the Jade Cord.
translations.idiomatic: Like polished ritual coral they shone; like stars on the Jade Cord they lit the age.
